plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing auctions you could have profitably won. With a value of $31, bidding exactly $31 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win whenever profitable and never overpay.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Since I win only when I have the highest value, and pay the second-highest bid (not my own), overbidding risks negative profit, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $46 to maximize expected profit in this single-round auction.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade the bid up or down—overbidding risks winning at a price above value, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $35, I should bid exactly $35 to maximize expected profit.
